title: Casey Winters on Growth Strategy, Search SEO Loops, and Marketplaces
content:
Lenny Rachitsky: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast. Today my guest is Casey Winters, former Chief Product Officer at Eventbrite and growth leader at Pinterest and Grubhub.

Casey Winters: Thanks Lenny, happy to be here.

Lenny Rachitsky: You have worked on some of the largest consumer platforms. What is your playbook for scaling marketplace liquidity?

Casey Winters: In two-sided marketplaces, supply and demand are rarely constrained equally. You must identify which side is the hard side of the market. For Grubhub, it was restaurant supply; for Eventbrite, it was event creators. Once you acquire the hard side, demand follows naturally through search loops and organic discovery.

Lenny Rachitsky: How has SEO content loop strategy evolved for modern products?

Casey Winters: High-performing SEO loops rely on user-generated content or programmatic data pages rather than manual blog publishing. Pinterest scaled by turning user pins into indexable visual landing pages. Grubhub indexed restaurant menus and review aggregations. When users create content as a natural byproduct of using your app, your SEO loop scales infinitely without linear editorial costs.
